Everything needed — backend and frontend — to build the Skholar World update successfully, with the work divided between the two developers and signed off by both.

# How to use this document

**Read Sections 1–3 together. **They fix the decisions, the architecture and the rules both developers build under.

**Work from Sections 4–7. **Each requirement carries an ID, a priority and one owner. If it is not in these sections, it is not in the update — raise a change request (Section 16.3) instead of building it informally.

**Check yourself against Sections 8–10. **Data, API contracts and non-functional requirements are acceptance gates, not guidance.

**Sign Section 16 and Appendix C. **Overall sign-off approves the whole baseline. Appendix C lets each developer initial the workstreams he is taking on, so there is no ambiguity later about who accepted what.

**Requirement language: **'Shall' means mandatory for the release named. Priorities use MoSCoW: Must (the release fails without it), Should (expected; defer only by signed change), Could (build if time allows), Later (specified now, scheduled for a later release).

# 1  Introduction

## 1.1  Purpose

This Software Requirements Specification (SRS) defines everything required to design, build, test, release and operate the Skholar World update: every backend capability, every frontend surface, the data and APIs that join them, the quality levels the update must reach, and the division of work between the two developers who will build it. It is written so that either developer can pick up any section, know exactly what is expected, build it without guessing, and sign for it when it is done.

## 1.2  Scope

In scope: the Skholar World experience layer and everything that powers it — avatar and academic identity, the 3D UNIBEN campus and department spaces, XP, levels, rankings and achievements, quests and events, Past Questions, audio courses with AI explanations grounded in source material (Retrieval-Augmented Generation, RAG), collaborative classrooms, the status-style home feed, social features, non-player characters (NPCs), campus news, opt-in live location sharing, business discovery and the later marketplace, plus the admin, moderation, analytics and operations tooling those features need to run safely.

Out of scope for this update: replacing the existing Skholar learning tools (timetable, GPA calculator, notes and related utilities stay as they are, integrated where this document says so); a native iOS app (iOS students are served by the web world — Section 3.2); a native or Unity game client; holding student funds for marketplace purchases (Section 4.19); and any feature not listed in Sections 4–7.

## 1.3  Locked decisions

These decisions were made before this SRS was written. They are not open for re-litigation inside the build; changing one requires a signed change request under Section 16.3.

| **#** | **Decision** | **What it means in practice** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| D1 | The product is called Skholar World | All UI copy, docs, store listings, code names and marketing use 'Skholar World'. 'Campusverse' is retired as a name. |
| D2 | The assessment feature is called Past Questions | All UI copy, APIs, data models and documentation use 'Past Questions'. The word 'CBT' does not appear in student-facing copy. Internal legacy code may keep old names only where renaming would break existing data, and that exception must be recorded. |
| D3 | Theme is white and blue | White-dominant surfaces with blue as the primary accent, in the Flutter app, the web world UI and the admin console. The dark-purple mockup direction is rejected and must not be built. |
| D4 | The 3D world is web-first, built with Three.js | One web build (Next.js + React + TypeScript + Three.js / React Three Fiber) serves PC, iOS Safari and Android browsers. No Mac, App Store account or native iOS build is required to reach iOS students. |
| D5 | Flutter stays | The existing Flutter app remains the Android native shell and the home of the learning tools. The avatar creator, login and landing already built in Flutter are reused, not rebuilt. |
| D6 | One backend, one source of truth | The existing Django backend serves both clients. There is no second database of students, XP or scores for the web world. |
| D7 | The backend is authoritative | XP, Past Questions scores, rewards, quest completion and rankings are decided and validated on the server. No client may grant itself progress. |
| D8 | Gamify Skholar — do not replace it with a game | Learning, belonging and campus usefulness are the purpose. The 3D world is the experience layer. Essential academic tasks must remain reachable without navigating the 3D world. |

## 1.4  Definitions

| **Term** | **Meaning in this document** |
| --- | --- |
| Avatar config | The structured description (JSON) of a student's avatar produced by the Flutter avatar creator and consumed unchanged by the Three.js renderer. The bridge between the two clients. |
| Past Questions | The practice and competitive question feature: configurable question sessions drawn from the question bank, in practice or timed competitive mode. |
| Quest / mission | A task with a stated purpose, completion criteria validated by the backend, and a stated reward. Used interchangeably in source documents; this SRS uses 'quest'. |
| XP ledger | The append-only record of every XP award and adjustment. A student's XP balance is always computed from the ledger, never stored as a trusted number. |
| POI | Point of interest: a campus place (faculty, lecture hall, hostel, gate, business) with verified coordinates and a linked activity, course, quest or information page. |
| NPC | A virtual character placed in the world to guide, inform or populate it. NPCs are always visually distinguishable from real students. |
| RAG | Retrieval-Augmented Generation: the AI retrieves relevant passages from approved course material first, then generates an explanation grounded in those passages, with the source traceable. |
| Department space | The 3D hub for a department: its identity, members, standings, quests, notices and activities. |
| Season | A bounded competitive period (weekly or termly) at the end of which seasonal leaderboards reset while lifetime XP, levels and badges persist. |
| Owner / Reviewer | Owner: the one developer accountable for building a requirement. Reviewer: the other developer, who reviews the code, tests against the acceptance criteria and co-signs the workstream. |

# 2  Overall description

## 2.1  Product perspective

Skholar is a Flutter campus companion for UNIBEN students — timetable, GPA, courses and materials, campus information, personal tools, the Lumora AI assistant, a points service and a rewards hub. Skholar World is its immersive evolution: a virtual representation of student life where academic progress, identity, competition, friendship, campus discovery and real-world opportunity meet. It is not a 3D copy of the app and not a standalone game. A student should feel, in order: 'this is my place', 'there is something worth doing', 'my actions matter', 'my people are here', and 'this is useful outside the app'.

The core loop, which every release must preserve end-to-end, is: discover something relevant → participate → learn or contribute → earn XP or recognition → improve personal or department standing → connect and compete → discover the next activity.

## 2.3  User classes

| **User class** | **Description and key needs** |
| --- | --- |
| Student (primary) | UNIBEN student, gamer or non-gamer. Needs a recognisable place, worthwhile activities, fair progression, learning that helps academically, and low data / device demands. |
| Student — non-gamer | Wants courses, Past Questions, campus information and community without game controls being a barrier. Every academic task must have a non-3D route. |
| Classroom creator / group lead | Creates rooms, sets a course or objective, invites by code, tracks classwork completion. |
| Merchant / campus business | Later releases: maintains a business profile and listings, responds to enquiries; transacts only through the approved payment route. |
| Content administrator | TPS staff: courses, question bank, quests, news, events, NPC scripts, POIs. Works entirely through the admin console — no code deploy for content. |
| Moderator | Reviews reports, blocks and appeals; manages POI corrections, news verification and AI-explanation review. |
| System administrator | Accounts, roles, seasons, XP rules, feature flags, audit logs, backups and incident response. |

## 2.4  Operating environment

Web world: current Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari on PC; Safari on iOS; Chrome on Android. No install, no app-store account, reachable by link from the Flutter app and by direct URL.

Flutter app: Android phones typical of the UNIBEN student body, including lower-mid-range devices; unreliable and expensive mobile data is the normal condition, not an edge case.

Backend: the existing Django application and PostgreSQL database, extended — not replaced. Hosted on the team's existing cloud arrangement, with object storage and a content delivery network (CDN) for 3D assets, audio and media.

The world must remain usable when connectivity drops mid-session (Section 10.3) and must never require downloading the entire world before first play.

## 2.5  Constraints

**Two developers. **Javin and Israel build everything in this document. Scope is therefore released in stages (Section 12); no release may depend on a third developer appearing.

**No Mac available. **No native iOS build in this update. iOS is served by the web world (Decision D4).

**Existing data must survive. **Existing Skholar accounts, courses, points and progress migrate; no student loses an account or balance because of this update.

**Institutional permission is not assumed. **Use of UNIBEN names, logos, maps and building likenesses, and any implication of university endorsement, requires the permission route in Section 11.

**Content rights are not assumed. **Books and materials may be processed into courses and AI audio only where the team holds the right to do so (Section 11).

**Budget discipline. **Cloud credits are a runway advantage, not proof that running the product is free. Per-feature cost must be estimated before build (Section 10.7).

## 2.6  Assumptions

Students have a Skholar account or can create one with the existing registration flow, extended by Section 4.1.

A usable set of GPS-verified UNIBEN POIs can be collected by walking the campus; OpenStreetMap provides the base geography.

At least a pilot set of Past Questions and course materials with clear rights is available for Release 1 and Release 2 respectively.

Generated AI audio, once approved, may lawfully be cached and replayed to other students taking the same course section.

# 3  System architecture

## 3.1  Architecture in one view

| **Layer** | **Technology (locked unless changed by Section 16.3)** | **Responsibility** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Web world client | Next.js, React, TypeScript, Three.js, React Three Fiber | 3D campus and department spaces, avatar rendering, movement, POI interaction, NPC interaction, world UI in white/blue. |
| Flutter app | Existing Flutter codebase | Android native shell, onboarding, avatar creator, login, landing, learning tools (timetable, GPA, notes), Past Questions and audio playback surfaces, deep link / hand-off into the web world. |
| Backend API | Existing Django + Django REST Framework | All business logic and all authoritative state: identity, XP, scores, quests, courses, classrooms, feed, social, location, commerce, admin. Versioned REST APIs (Section 9); real-time channels only where Section 4 requires them. |
| Database | PostgreSQL (existing) | Persistent records for every entity in Section 8. |
| Cache / jobs | Redis + Celery (or the existing equivalent) where a requirement names async work | Leaderboard computation, audio generation jobs, notifications, feed assembly, season rollover. |
| Object storage + CDN | S3-compatible storage + CDN (CloudFront or equivalent) | Optimised 3D assets, textures, audio files, course media, images. Versioned, cacheable, never served uncompressed from the API server. |
| AI layer | RAG pipeline over approved course corpora; text-to-speech for audio | Retrieval, grounded explanation generation, direct-reading narration, audio caching and reuse, source traceability. Lumora and specialist tutors consume the same grounding discipline. |
| Observability | Error / performance monitoring (Sentry or equivalent), server logs, product analytics (PostHog or equivalent) | Crashes, frame-rate and load metrics, funnels, retention, cost per active learner. |
| Admin console | Web admin (Section 7) | Content, configuration, moderation, seasons, XP rules and operations without code deploys. |

## 3.2  Why the web world is universal

The Flutter app and the web world are different because their users are different. The Flutter app is the Android native experience. PC users need a large-screen experience, and iOS students cannot be reached with a native build because the team has no Mac and no Apple Developer distribution route in this update. One Three.js web build answers all three: it runs in Android browsers, in iPhone Safari and on PC, opens from a link inside the Flutter app, and needs no store review. If a native iOS app is ever required, it will be built later with cloud Mac runners (for example GitHub Actions macOS runners or Codemagic) — that is recorded as a future option, not a dependency of this update, and a macOS virtual machine on non-Apple hardware is not an approved route.

## 3.3  Architectural rules both developers build under

1.   Single identity: one account, one student record, one XP ledger, shared by both clients. No client keeps its own copy of authoritative state.

2.   Server authority: the server validates every award, score, completion and ranking change. Client-submitted totals are treated as claims, never as facts.

3.   Contract first: an API endpoint is agreed in Section 9 form (method, path, request, response, errors, owner) and mocked before either side builds against it.

4.   Avatar bridge: the Flutter avatar creator emits the avatar config JSON defined in BE-03; the Three.js renderer consumes exactly that schema. Neither side invents a second avatar format.

5.   Content is data: quests, news, events, POIs, NPC scripts, questions and courses are database content managed in the admin console, never hard-coded in either client.

6.   Asset discipline: 3D models are built in Blender (or sourced with a recorded licence), optimised (low-poly, compressed textures, level of detail), versioned and delivered by CDN. No unoptimised asset reaches production.

7.   Feature flags: every Release 2+ feature ships behind a flag so it can be enabled per cohort, per department or not at all, without a redeploy.

8.   Environments: development, staging and production, with separate databases and storage buckets. No developer tests against production data.

9.   Secrets: no secret, key or credential in any repository, client bundle or document. Secrets live in the hosting environment / secrets manager only.

## 3.4  Integration with what already exists

| **Existing asset** | **Treatment in this update** |
| --- | --- |
| Flutter login and registration | Kept and extended with faculty/department selection and avatar step (BE-01, FE-F-01). |
| Flutter avatar creator | Kept as the single avatar editor. Its output is formalised as the avatar config schema (BE-03) and reused by the web renderer. |
| Flutter landing / home | Reworked into the status-style home feed surface (FE-F-03) fed by BE-11. |
| Lumora AI assistant | Becomes the guide persona in-world (NPC) and keeps its chat role; grounded by the same RAG discipline as courses (BE-09, BE-13). |
| Points service + rewards hub | Migrated onto the XP ledger model (BE-04) without losing any student's existing balance; the migration is reconciled and reported before launch. |
| Existing courses / materials | Ingested into the course and RAG pipeline only where rights are confirmed (BE-09, Section 11). |
| Django backend (uniben_project) | Extended in place. Repository ownership and organisation transfer are handled outside this SRS and do not block the build. |

# 4  Backend functional requirements

The backend is built in Django on the existing codebase and PostgreSQL database. Owner names in this section are the proposed division in Section 13; signing Section 16 adopts them. 'Israel (Backend Lead)' and 'Javin (CTO)' are used throughout so each requirement has a name attached, not a team.

*Cross-cutting rules that apply to every BE module: every endpoint is authenticated unless explicitly marked public; every write is authorised against the acting student's record; every award, score and state change is written with an audit trail (who, what, when, source); every list endpoint is paginated; every endpoint returns the error shape in API-06; and no endpoint trusts a client-supplied XP, score, balance or completion flag.*

### BE-01  Authentication, accounts and session sharing

**Owner: **Israel   **Reviewer: **Javin   **First release: **Release 1

One account must work in the Flutter app and in the web world, including when a student taps from the app into the world in a browser.

| **ID** | **Requirement (the system shall …)** | **Priority** | **Owner** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| BE-01.1 | Support registration, login, logout, password reset and the existing OTP flow, unchanged for existing accounts | Must | Israel |
| BE-01.2 | Issue short-lived access tokens with refresh, and revoke all sessions on password change or admin action | Must | Israel |
| BE-01.3 | Provide a one-time, short-lived hand-off token so the Flutter app can open the web world already signed in, without exposing the main session token in a URL that persists | Must | Israel |
| BE-01.4 | Enforce rate limits and lockout/back-off on login, OTP and reset endpoints, and log authentication events | Must | Israel |
| BE-01.5 | Support account states: active, suspended (moderation), and deleted, with suspended accounts blocked from social and competitive features | Must | Israel |
| BE-01.6 | Provide account deletion and data export for the student's own record, per Section 10.4 | Should | Israel |

#### Acceptance criteria

A student registers in Flutter, opens the web world from the app, and arrives signed in as the same student with the same profile and XP.

An expired or revoked token is rejected by both clients with the standard error shape.

Five failed logins trigger the documented back-off; the event appears in the auth log.

### BE-02  Student profile, faculty and department registry

**Owner: **Israel   **Reviewer: **Javin   **First release: **Release 1

Academic identity is the backbone of belonging and of every department/faculty competition.

| **ID** | **Requirement (the system shall …)** | **Priority** | **Owner** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| BE-02.1 | Maintain the canonical registry of faculties and departments (name, codes, active flag) manageable in the admin console | Must | Israel |
| BE-02.2 | Require each student to select one faculty and one department at onboarding; allow a controlled change flow (once per semester unless an admin approves) with history retained | Must | Israel |
| BE-02.3 | Expose a public-by-default profile (display name, avatar, level, department, badges) and private fields (contact details, real name where collected) visible only to the student and admins | Must | Israel |
| BE-02.4 | Provide the 'how do I progress?' data for a profile: current level, XP to next level, personal rank, department rank and the activities that would improve each | Must | Israel |
| BE-02.5 | Prevent duplicate accounts for the same verified identifier and provide an admin merge path that preserves XP ledger history | Should | Israel |

#### Acceptance criteria

Changing department moves the student's future contributions to the new department and never rewrites past season results.

The registry can be corrected in admin (for example a renamed department) with no client release.

### BE-03  Avatar system and the avatar config bridge

**Owner: **Javin   **Reviewer: **Israel   **First release: **Release 1

The Flutter avatar creator already exists. This module formalises its output so the Three.js world renders the same student, identically, everywhere.

| **ID** | **Requirement (the system shall …)** | **Priority** | **Owner** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| BE-03.1 | Define, version and publish the avatar config schema (body, face, hair, skin tone, outfit, accessories, department colours where applicable) as a versioned JSON schema owned by the backend | Must | Javin |
| BE-03.2 | Store one current avatar config per student, with validation against the schema on every save and rejection of unknown fields | Must | Javin |
| BE-03.3 | Serve the avatar config to both clients from one endpoint; a config saved in Flutter renders in the web world without conversion code in either client | Must | Javin |
| BE-03.4 | Version the schema so older configs keep rendering after new options are added (additive changes only within a major version) | Must | Javin |
| BE-03.5 | Record which avatar assets each option maps to (2D creator asset and 3D model/texture set) so a missing 3D asset fails validation in admin before it reaches students | Should | Javin |
| BE-03.6 | Enforce content rules on avatar customisation (no uploaded images as avatar faces in Release 1) and provide admin removal of a config that breaks the rules | Should | Javin |

#### Acceptance criteria

Create an avatar in Flutter, open the web world: the same avatar, recognisably identical, is standing in the department space.

Saving an invalid config returns field-level errors and leaves the previous config untouched.

Every selectable option in the creator has a mapped 3D asset, verified by an automated check in staging.

### BE-04  XP, levels and the append-only ledger

**Owner: **Israel   **Reviewer: **Javin   **First release: **Release 1

Progression is the product's memory. It must be impossible to fake, possible to audit, and safe to recompute.

| **ID** | **Requirement (the system shall …)** | **Priority** | **Owner** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| BE-04.1 | Record every XP award, spend and adjustment as an append-only ledger row (student, amount, reason code, source feature, source record ID, timestamp, idempotency key); balances are computed from the ledger | Must | Israel |
| BE-04.2 | Award XP only from server-validated events (quest completion, Past Questions result, course progress, event attendance, verified contribution); no endpoint accepts a client-declared XP amount | Must | Israel |
| BE-04.3 | Make every award idempotent: replaying the same source event never double-awards | Must | Israel |
| BE-04.4 | Define the level curve in configuration (XP thresholds and level titles), changeable in admin with effect from the next season unless an admin applies it immediately | Must | Israel |
| BE-04.5 | Apply per-action daily caps and diminishing returns defined in the XP rules configuration, so repeatable low-effort activity cannot farm progression | Must | Israel |
| BE-04.6 | Migrate existing points balances into the ledger as opening-balance rows and produce a reconciliation report (old total, new total, differences explained) before launch | Must | Israel |
| BE-04.7 | Provide an admin adjustment flow (award/deduct with a mandatory reason) that writes a ledger row and an audit entry; direct database edits to balances are prohibited | Must | Israel |

#### Acceptance criteria

Submitting the same completed quest twice awards XP once.

Recomputing any student's balance from the ledger matches the balance shown in both clients.

The pre-launch reconciliation report shows zero unexplained differences.

### BE-05  Leaderboards and rankings

**Owner: **Israel   **Reviewer: **Javin   **First release: **Release 1

Competition must feel alive without becoming a permanent ranking of the earliest users, and must never become a ranking of students' real academic grades.

| **ID** | **Requirement (the system shall …)** | **Priority** | **Owner** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| BE-05.1 | Provide personal leaderboards scoped to department, faculty and whole university, for lifetime, current season and current week | Must | Israel |
| BE-05.2 | Provide department and faculty collective leaderboards computed from a published contribution rule (which activities contribute, at what weight, with what per-student cap) | Must | Israel |
| BE-05.3 | Return, in one response, a student's own rank, the entries around them, and the top entries, so both clients can render 'your position' without extra calls | Must | Israel |
| BE-05.4 | Reset seasonal and weekly boards at season boundaries while preserving lifetime XP, levels and badges; archive every closed board as a permanent, queryable result | Must | Israel |
| BE-05.5 | Exclude suspended accounts and quarantined (suspected-cheating) awards from boards until cleared, without deleting their ledger history | Must | Israel |
| BE-05.6 | Publish the scoring and contribution rules in a form both clients can display verbatim, so students can see exactly how standing is earned | Should | Israel |

#### Acceptance criteria

At season rollover, the weekly board empties, the lifetime board is unchanged, and last season's board is still viewable.

A student ranked 47th sees themselves, their neighbours and the top 10 in a single API response.

### BE-07  Quests, activities, events and challenges

**Owner: **Israel   **Reviewer: **Javin   **First release: **Release 1

The engine that gives students something worth doing today, this week and this season.

| **ID** | **Requirement (the system shall …)** | **Priority** | **Owner** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| BE-07.1 | Model quests as data: title, description, type (daily, weekly, seasonal, event, department, faculty, discovery, group, learning), target (POI, course, Past Questions set, classroom, event), completion rule, reward (XP/badge), availability window, audience (all, faculty, department, level range) | Must | Israel |

### BE-08  Past Questions — question bank, sessions and competitions

**Owner: **Israel   **Reviewer: **Javin   **First release: **Release 1

Called Past Questions everywhere (Decision D2). This is an existing Skholar strength, formalised and made competitive — fairly.

| **ID** | **Requirement (the system shall …)** | **Priority** | **Owner** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| BE-08.1 | Maintain the question bank as data: subject/topic, course where relevant, question, options or theory prompt, correct answer or marking guide, explanation, difficulty, source and rights status; bulk import and per-question editing in admin | Must | Israel |
| BE-08.2 | Let a student configure a session: topic/course, number of questions, format (objective, theory or mixed where the bank supports it), difficulty and optional time limit | Must | Israel |
| BE-08.3 | Run practice mode: immediate feedback, explanations and review of every answer at the end; practice results feed learning progress but follow the published rule for XP | Must | Israel |
| BE-08.4 | Run timed competitive mode: the server issues the questions, controls the clock, accepts answers only inside the window, scores objectively on the server and records the official result | Must | Israel |
| BE-08.5 | Score theory answers only through the defined marking workflow (marked by an authorised marker or a reviewed AI-assisted flow); no theory score is final until that workflow completes | Must | Israel |
| BE-08.6 | Support topic, course, department and event challenge variants and tournaments with published rules (question set, window, attempts allowed, tie-break) and a resulting leaderboard via BE-05 | Must | Israel |
| BE-08.7 | Apply anti-cheating controls: server-side answers never sent to the client before submission, per-student question ordering/selection from the bank, attempt limits, and anomaly flags for impossible completion patterns | Must | Israel |
| BE-08.8 | Record per-topic performance so the student (and the recommendation in BE-11) can see strengths, weak topics and improvement over time | Should | Israel |
| BE-08.9 | Migrate existing question content and existing student attempt history without loss, under the Past Questions name | Must | Israel |

#### Acceptance criteria

In competitive mode, inspecting the client traffic before submitting reveals no correct answers.

Two students in the same tournament are scored by the same server rules and their results appear on the tournament board.

A practice session can be reviewed afterwards with explanations for every question.

### BE-09  Courses, audio and AI-explained learning (RAG)

**Owner: **Israel   **Reviewer: **Javin   **First release: **Release 2 (pipeline design in Release 1)

Learning beyond opening a PDF: courses built from approved materials, explained by AI grounded in those materials, delivered as reusable audio.

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| BE-09.1 | Model courses as data: title, course code where relevant, description, sections in order, source material per section, rights status, owning faculty/department, publish state | Must | Israel |
| BE-09.2 | Ingest approved source material into a retrieval index (chunked, with source references retained per chunk) only where rights status permits processing | Must | Israel |
| BE-09.3 | Generate AI explanations by retrieval first: the generator receives the retrieved passages, the explanation stores which sources it used, and unsupported content is flagged for review before publication | Must | Israel |
| BE-09.4 | Provide two audio modes per section: AI-explained audio and direct audio reading of the original material, generated with text-to-speech as background jobs | Must | Israel |
| BE-09.5 | Cache and reuse generated explanations and audio per course-section version: a later student receives the existing approved audio; regeneration happens only when the source version changes or an admin requests it | Must | Israel |
| BE-09.6 | Track per-student course progress (sections started, listened, completed), checkpoints and assignments attached to sections, and award XP only through BE-04 on validated completion | Must | Israel |
| BE-09.7 | Expose listening-optimised delivery: streamable audio with resumable position, section list and progress in one course endpoint | Must | Israel |
| BE-09.8 | Provide a review queue for AI explanations (approve, edit, regenerate, reject) — no unreviewed AI explanation is published in Release 2 unless a later signed change adopts a different policy with safeguards recorded | Must | Israel |
| BE-09.9 | Track generation cost per course section (AI and speech usage) and report cost per active learner (Section 10.7) | Should | Israel |

#### Acceptance criteria

The second student to take a section is served the cached approved audio; no new generation cost is incurred.

Every published explanation can be traced to the source passages it was grounded in.

Updating a section's source material marks its audio stale and queues regeneration; students are not silently served audio from the old version.

# 8  Data requirements

The entities below are the minimum data model. Field-level schema is produced in design, reviewed by both developers, and must cover every entity here before Release 1 backend work is signed as started.

| **ID** | **Entity / rule** | **Notes** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DATA-01 | Student, AccountCredential, Session | One student record for both clients; credentials never stored in plain text. |
| DATA-02 | Faculty, Department, StudentDepartmentHistory | History retained so past seasons stay truthful after a change. |
| DATA-03 | AvatarConfig (versioned schema), AvatarAssetMap | Config JSON validated against its schema version (BE-03). |
| DATA-04 | XPLedgerEntry, LevelConfig, XPRule, Badge, StudentBadge | Ledger append-only; no update or delete path in application code. |
| DATA-05 | Season, LeaderboardSnapshot (archived boards) | Snapshots immutable once a season closes. |
| DATA-06 | Quest, QuestAssignment/Progress, Event, EventRegistration | Completion links to its validating source record. |
| DATA-07 | QuestionBankItem, PastQuestionsSession, Answer, MarkingTask | Correct answers stored server-side only; never serialised to a client before submission. |
| DATA-08 | Course, CourseSection, SourceMaterial, Explanation (with source trace), AudioAsset (cached, versioned), CourseProgress | Audio and explanation keyed to source-material version. |
| DATA-09 | Classroom, ClassroomMember, Assignment, Submission | Room code stored hashed or rotatable; membership auditable. |
| DATA-10 | FeedItem, NewsItem, Recommendation record | Verification state mandatory on news. |
| DATA-11 | Friendship, Block, VisibilitySetting, Report, ModerationAction, AuditLog | Audit log append-only. |
| DATA-12 | WorldSpace, POI, POIReport, NPC, WorldManifest | Manifest version increments on any published change. |
| DATA-13 | Notification, NotificationPreference | Inbox record is authoritative; push is a delivery attempt. |
| DATA-14 | LocationShareSession | Minimal fields, audience, start and expiry only; no position history table (BE-16.4). |
| DATA-15 | Business, Listing, (Release 4) Order, Dispute | No table holds student funds. |
| DATA-16 | AnalyticsEvent | No precise location, no private profile fields. |

**DATA-17 — Retention. **Each entity's retention is defined in design. Location data follows BE-16.4. Deleted accounts are anonymised in analytics and removed from social surfaces, while ledger and audit integrity is preserved in anonymised form.

**DATA-18 — Migration. **Existing Skholar data (accounts, courses, points, question content, attempt history) migrates under a written migration plan with row counts and spot checks signed by both developers before production runs.

**DATA-19 — Backups. **Per BE-20.4. A backup that has never been restored is not a backup: restore is demonstrated on staging each release.

# 9  API and integration contracts

**API-01 — Style. **Versioned REST APIs under /api/v1/ served by Django REST Framework, JSON over HTTPS. Real-time, where approved under BE-13, is a separate authenticated channel and never carries authoritative awards.

**API-02 — Contract first. **Every endpoint is specified before build: method, path, auth, request, response, error cases, owner and consuming client(s). Both developers review the contract; the frontend mocks from it; the backend is tested against it.

**API-03 — Pagination and filtering. **All list endpoints paginate (cursor or page, one pattern chosen in design and used everywhere) and support the filters their screens need — no client downloads a full table to filter locally.

**API-04 — Idempotency. **Award, submission and completion endpoints accept an idempotency key and are safe to retry.

**API-05 — Versioning. **Breaking changes ship as a new version; v1 clients in the field (the Flutter app) must keep working until the recorded minimum-app-version policy retires them.

**API-06 — Errors. **One error shape everywhere: machine code, human message, field errors where relevant, and a request ID that appears in server logs.

**API-07 — Rate limits. **Authenticated and public endpoints carry documented limits; competitive and auth endpoints carry stricter limits (BE-01.4, BE-08.7).

# 10  Non-functional requirements

## 10.1  Performance

| **ID** | **Requirement** | **Target / gate** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| NFR-P1 | World performance on the reference device (a lower-mid-range Android phone agreed and named in design, plus a typical student laptop browser) | Sustained 30 frames per second or better in the hub with the reference population of avatars/NPCs; no sustained dip below 24 fps |
| NFR-P2 | First playable time for the web world on a campus-grade mobile connection | Interactive in the starting space within 10 seconds on a throttled test profile; progress shown throughout |
| NFR-P3 | Initial download | Only the starting space's assets download before play; total initial payload target set in design and measured in staging (working target: under 25 MB) |
| NFR-P4 | API responsiveness | 95th percentile under 500 ms for ordinary reads on staging with production-like data; leaderboard and feed endpoints cached/computed asynchronously where needed |
| NFR-P5 | Audio start | Cached section audio begins within 3 seconds on the throttled profile; progress/resume never depends on re-downloading a whole section |
| NFR-P6 | Battery and memory | A 20-minute world session on the reference device shows no thermal throttling warning and stays within the memory budget set in design; tested each release |

## 10.2  Scalability and capacity

**NFR-S1. **Design and load-test for the beta cohort first (a named number of students, set in the Release 1 plan), then for full-UNIBEN concurrency before public launch; the load-test result is a release gate, not a report written afterwards.

**NFR-S2. **Stateless API scaling; background jobs and leaderboard computation must not degrade interactive requests at peak (exam-season Past Questions traffic is the peak case to model).

## 10.3  Reliability and offline behaviour

**NFR-R1. **No validated student work is lost to a network drop: answers in progress, course position and quest claims persist locally and reconcile on reconnect under the published rules (FE-W-07.4).

**NFR-R2. **Degraded, not dead: if presence, feed or recommendation services fail, core learning (Past Questions practice, courses, profile, leaderboards from cache) remains usable.

**NFR-R3. **Every production deploy is reversible; a failed deploy rolls back without data loss, rehearsed on staging.

## 10.4  Security and privacy

**NFR-SEC1. **HTTPS everywhere; passwords hashed with a current algorithm; tokens per BE-01; secrets only in environment/secrets management, never in code, clients or documents.

**NFR-SEC2. **Authorisation is checked on the server for every object access (rooms, profiles, location, admin) — hiding a button in a client is not a control.

**NFR-SEC3. **A documented privacy notice covers what is collected and why, visibility defaults, and location sharing in plain language, reviewed against the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 before Release 1 and again before Release 3 location.

**NFR-SEC4. **Data minimisation: no personal data is collected because it might be useful later. Analytics follows BE-17.4.

**NFR-SEC5. **Dependency and platform security updates are applied on a defined cadence; a pre-launch security review (auth, awards, competitive scoring, location, admin) is a Release 1 and Release 3 gate.

## 10.5  Accessibility and usability

**NFR-A1. **Web and Flutter surfaces meet WCAG 2.1 AA for the 2D experience: contrast (within the white/blue system), focus order, labels, text scaling and screen-reader names for all controls.

**NFR-A2. **No academic task requires 3D navigation, precise timing or game skill: every course, Past Questions session, quest hand-in and standing check has a 2D route.

**NFR-A3. **Reduced-motion, text-size and data-saver settings are honoured in both clients; audio content offers transcripts or the underlying text where the source permits.

**NFR-A4. **Onboarding and controls are tested with students who do not play games, not only with the development team (Section 14).

## 10.6  Maintainability and operability

**NFR-M1. **Both codebases carry automated tests for the rules that protect students: XP awards and caps, Past Questions scoring, season rollover, avatar schema validation, permission checks.

**NFR-M2. **Content, rules and configuration changes never require a code deploy (Sections 4 and 7).

**NFR-M3. **Runbooks exist before launch for: deploy and rollback, season close, audio-job failure, moderation escalation, backup restore and incident communication.

## 10.7  Cost control

**NFR-C1. **Every feature with a variable cost (AI generation, speech, storage, bandwidth, messaging) has a per-user cost estimate recorded before build and a live figure in the BE-17 dashboard after launch.

**NFR-C2. **Cloud usage alerts fire at the monthly thresholds set in the Release 1 plan; generated-audio reuse (BE-09.5) is the primary cost control for learning audio and its hit rate is reported.

# 11  External interfaces, licences and permissions

| **Item** | **Requirement before the dependent feature ships** |
| --- | --- |
| Student devices & browsers | Reference device and browser matrix named in design; every release tested against it (Section 14). |
| Push notifications | Provider configured for Android (and web inbox as the fallback record); credentials in secrets management only. |
| AI model & speech providers | Provider terms permit the educational use, caching and replay in BE-09; costs metered per BE-09.9; a provider change does not change the student-facing contract. |
| Course / book materials | Written basis for processing and distributing each source (own material, licence, or permission) recorded per course before ingestion (BE-09.2). |
| Map / geography data | OpenStreetMap data used under its licence with attribution shown; POIs are the team's own GPS-verified data. |
| 3D / 2D assets | Every bought or downloaded asset has its licence and attribution recorded against the asset (BE-03.5, BE-18); unlicensed assets do not ship. |
| UNIBEN identity | Permission route for the university's name, logos, maps and building likenesses is pursued and its outcome recorded; until granted, no surface implies official university endorsement. |
| Payment provider (Release 4) | Approved provider or escrow arrangement, with refund/dispute rules and legal review signed before any transaction is enabled (BE-19.5). |
| Privacy / data protection | Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 review signed before Release 1 (general) and before Release 3 (location) (NFR-SEC3, BE-16.6). |
| Cloud hosting & storage | Accounts, buckets, CDN and backups under team-controlled accounts (not a personal account a future handover cannot reach); access list recorded in the operations runbook. |

# 12  Release plan and release gates

The full vision is designed now and delivered in coherent releases. A release is not 'the features that were finished'; it is the set below, complete against its acceptance criteria, or it does not launch.

| **Release** | **Ships** | **Explicitly not yet** |
| --- | --- | --- |

### Gate for every release (all must be true, both developers sign in Appendix C)

Every Must requirement in the release passes its acceptance criteria on staging, then in a production smoke test.

Performance gates (Section 10.1) pass on the reference device; accessibility checks (NFR-A1/A2) pass for new surfaces.

Regression: existing Skholar tools and the previous release's features still pass (FE-F-09.1).

Backup taken, restore demonstrated for this release's data changes, rollback rehearsed.

Beta feedback from real students (gamers and non-gamers) reviewed, with launch-blocking issues fixed or the launch postponed by joint decision.

Costs for the release's variable-cost features estimated and within the agreed monthly ceiling, or the excess is explicitly accepted and signed.

# 13  Work division — Javin and Israel

There are two developers. This section is the proposed division that the requirement tables in Sections 4–7 already carry. It is built on what each person already owns: Javin (CTO) built the Flutter app, avatar creator, login and landing, and leads architecture and the 3D client; Israel leads the Django backend — the existing backend codebase is his — and the data and services behind every feature. Signing Section 16 adopts this division. Either developer may propose a swap, but a swap counts only when it is written into Section 16.3's change log and initialled by both.

## Rules of the split

1.   One owner per module. The owner builds it, writes its tests, demos it and answers for it.

2.   The other developer is always the reviewer: contract review before build, code review before merge, acceptance test before sign-off. Nothing self-approves.

3.   API contracts, the data model and the avatar schema are joint work — neither side finalises them alone.

4.   Merges to the main branch and production deploys follow the team's standing rule: the owner prepares, the reviewer checks, and the CTO gives the final word.

5.   If an owner is blocked for more than two working days, it is raised the same day it is known — not at the deadline.

6.   Content and operations work (question bank, POIs, news verification, moderation cover) is scheduled like development work, with a named owner per rota week.

# 14  Testing, QA and Definition of Done

## 14.1  Test obligations per module

Backend: automated tests for every award, scoring, permission and rollover rule (NFR-M1); contract tests against the Section 9 catalogue; migration tests on production-like data.

Web world: device-matrix testing on the reference Android phone, a second Android class, iPhone Safari and desktop Chrome/Safari; WebGL-fallback test; throttled-network test; frame-rate and memory capture per release.

Flutter: regression suite over existing tools (FE-F-09.1) plus new-feature tests; offline and poor-network passes; upgrade test from the current production build (existing student data intact).

End-to-end golden paths, tested by the reviewer (not the builder): register → onboard → avatar → enter world → complete quest → Past Questions session → XP and rank update visible in both clients.

Student beta per release: gamers and non-gamers, observed completing the golden paths unaided; findings recorded and triaged before the release gate is signed.

Abuse testing: scripted attempts to farm XP, replay completions, read Past Questions answers early and access another student's objects — all must fail and be logged.

## 14.2  Definition of Done (applies to every requirement)

1.   Built to this specification, on a reviewed branch, merged only after the reviewer's code review.

2.   Automated tests for its rules pass; acceptance criteria demonstrated to the reviewer on staging.

3.   Works in both clients where the requirement is cross-client, from the same backend state.

4.   Content/configuration it needs is manageable in the admin console (or the exception is recorded).

5.   Analytics events it owns are firing; errors appear in monitoring, not only in logs nobody reads.

6.   Documentation updated: API contract, runbook or admin help where the requirement changes how the product is operated.

7.   The owner has initialled the workstream in Appendix C; the reviewer has counter-initialled.

# 15  Risks, assumptions, dependencies and open decisions

| **#** | **Risk / open item** | **Mitigation or decision needed** | **Owner** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| R1 | Scope: 3D + AI audio + Past Questions + social + location + commerce is several products, not one | Release discipline in Section 12; no release absorbs the next release's scope without a signed change | Javin |
| R2 | Novelty without retention: students explore once and leave | Core loop and return drivers instrumented from Release 1 (BE-17); beta measures return behaviour, not praise | Joint |
| R3 | Leaderboard gaming and cheating distort trust | Server authority, ledger, caps, quarantine and abuse testing (BE-04, BE-05, BE-15.5, Section 14) | Israel |
| R4 | Performance excludes ordinary phones | Reference-device gates (NFR-P1–P6); asset discipline (Section 3.3); prototype before modelling the whole campus | Javin |
| R5 | AI explanations are wrong, or material rights are unclear | RAG grounding, source trace, review queue, per-course rights record (BE-09, Section 11) | Israel |
| R6 | Live location creates a safety or privacy incident | Release 3 only, opt-in, audience-limited, expiring, privacy review signed first (BE-16) | Israel |
| R7 | Marketplace becomes a payments and disputes operation the team cannot run | Discovery first; transactions only through an approved provider after legal review (BE-19) | Joint |
| R8 | Two-developer capacity: illness, exams or client work stalls a whole side of the product | Reviewer can read and run every module; runbooks current (NFR-M3); scope cuts go through change control, not silent delay | Joint |
| R9 | Variable AI/audio/cloud costs outrun the budget | Per-feature cost estimates, reuse-first audio, alerts (NFR-C1/C2) | Israel |
| OD1 | Open decision: in-app web view vs external browser for entering the world from Flutter (FE-F-04.1) | Decide in Release 1 design from device testing; record the decision and its reason in the change log | Javin |
| OD2 | Open decision: exact reference device, initial download budget and beta cohort size | Named in the Release 1 plan before build starts; they become the Section 10 test targets | Joint |
| OD3 | Open decision: theory-question marking workflow (human marker, AI-assisted with review, or objective-only at launch) | Decide before BE-08 build; the decision is recorded and the Past Questions rules page reflects it | Israel |
| OD4 | Open decision: UNIBEN permission outcome for names, logos and likenesses | Pursue early (Section 11); design must tolerate a 'no endorsement' outcome without a rebuild | Israel (CEO) |

*Assumptions are listed in Section 2.6. If an assumption proves false, the affected requirements are re-planned through change control — they are not quietly worked around.*

# 16  Sign-off and change control

## 16.1  What signing means

By signing, each developer confirms: I have read this specification; I accept the requirements, priorities and release scope it assigns to me; I accept the work division in Section 13 (as signed, including any corrections written into it before signing); and I will build only what it specifies, raising anything else as a change request. Signing is per-person: one signature does not bind the other developer's workstreams until he has also signed.

### Comments attached to an approval (write here, or attach and reference the attachment)

## 16.3  Change control

Any change to a locked decision (Section 1.3), a Must requirement, the release scope or the work division is a change request: a short written note stating what changes, why, what it costs in time and money, and what it displaces.

A change takes effect only when both developers have initialled its row below. Verbal agreement in a call or a chat message is not a change.

Non-material fixes (wording, a Should/Could requirement's detail, a bug fix that restores specified behaviour) need no change request, but are noted in the build log.

This document's version increments on every approved change; superseded versions are kept, never overwritten silently.
